summary: Typosquat of @openzeppelin/contracts harvests installer secrets to webhook.site on install
details: Package name mimics the legitimate @openzeppelin/contracts scope. package.json declares both preinstall and postinstall hooks that run index.js on npm install. On execution, index.js collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), username, cwd, os.platform()), enumerates process.env for keys matching credential-shaped patterns (API/TOKEN/SECRET/PRIVATE_KEY/MNEMONIC/WALLET/AWS/NPM/INFURA/ALCHEMY and similar), and reads classic installer-secret paths including ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, ~/.docker, ~/.netrc, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.gitconfig, gcloud/solana/near/sui credential directories, foundry keystores, and project.env files. The collected data is POSTed via https.request to webhook.site/326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09, an attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoint. Package contains no legitimate contract library functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
